newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GAS COMPANY POSTPONES SHAREHOLDERS' MEETING.
newsitem.headline: GAS COMPANY POSTPONES SHAREHOLDERS' MEETING.

text.p: Lithuanian Gas said on Monday that its general shareholders' meeting, originally scheduled for today, had been postponsed for two weeks due to a disagreement with auditor Coopers & Lybrand.

"We are postponing our general shareholders' for around two weeks because our interpretation of profit tax calculation methods differ from those of Coopers & Lybrand," the firm's director general Kestutis Shumacheris told Reuters.
Shumacheris confirmed earlier reports that the company's 1996 audited losses were at least 79 million litas.
"The losses might be even bigger," he said.
The losses stemmed from overdue payments for supplies in 1992 and 1993, Shumacheris said.
The delayed payments were caused by the difference between what the company paid for its supplies and what it charged to consumers.
"The government is looking for sources to compensate us...and we expect that it will decide either to issue new shares, use budgetary sources, or raise gas prices," Shumacheris said.
Lithuanian Gas is about 90 percent state-owned and its private shares are traded on the A list of the Vilnius bourse.
